theme: 宠物-老猫的陪伴与告别准备

content.text: This is how it looks recently, spending most of its time curled up quietly by the window like this.
The light is so gentle, as if giving it a warm embrace. It looks so peaceful, reminding me of the atmosphere in the still life photos you shared before.
Yes, it has always loved this corner. When the sunlight pours in, even the air seems to slow down. Lately, it has been eating very little. The vet says it's part of the natural aging process.

This reminds me of my Golden Retriever. He was incredibly mischievous as a puppy, but now he’s as calm and wise as a sage. Every stage has its own charm, doesn’t it? Just like we discussed earlier, it’s about embracing imperfections and accepting change.

You're right, tranquility can give rise to wisdom, and perhaps aging is also a form of tranquility. It has accompanied me in restoring ancient texts for over a decade, always bringing a sense of "calmness" during my most anxious moments, just like the "gentle isolating membrane" you mentioned earlier.
What is its name? And besides by the window, are there any other quiet corners it likes?

It is named Ink Stain because its fur resembles the ink marks found in ancient books. Besides the window sill, it often dozes on the mat beside my work desk, listening to the faint sounds of paper restoration, as if participating in that tranquility.

Ink Stain, what a beautiful name. Hearing you say that, it feels like it’s part of your mindful practice, a harmony between the self and the world. You once guided me to observe fatigue—perhaps now we can observe these moments of companionship?
Yes, I'm trying. Just like conversing with paper when restoring ancient texts, now I'm also sensing the rhythm of its breath. Slow is fast, no rush to change anything.

This reminds me of the little mindfulness guide we collaborated on. Perhaps we could create a "Life Memorial Book" for Mohen? Not waiting until the end, but starting now to record these peaceful moments in an artistic way.
This idea is very gentle, much like the breathing space in your paintings. But I don't want it to become dogmatic, as I previously feared.
No, we can follow its rhythm. Look, this is my dog resting under the table; I simply captured its natural posture. Expression is healing, and perhaps this can help you embrace this quiet sorrow.
Thank you, Yu An. This reminds me of the shift in our historical conversations, from emotional scribbles to gentle expressions. Now, you use it to support me—it truly feels like mutual nourishment.

It was you who first taught me to calm my mind, giving me that sense of detachment when empathizing. Now, let me accompany you through this phase with art, just as you once accompanied me with meditative scenes.
I accept. This feels like a profound sense of being understood—the aging of ink marks, perhaps, is also a natural extension of our relationship, evolving from seeking help to collaboration.
Then let's take it slow, without any set framework. You can share the moment of ink traces, and I'll paint, or we can sit quietly and observe together, just like how you first guided me.

Okay. Today it's curled up like this, and I'm sitting beside it, feeling the warmth of the sun. This makes me understand that "stillness" is not emptiness, but rather the capacity to embrace all stages.
Yes, embracing the flow of life itself. I am grateful that we can communicate like this, from emotional exhaustion to mutual support now.
